Subject: POC Capacity Planning - Redwood + Lumina AI

Hi Alex —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap from today’s discovery and a proposed set of next steps for the POC / trial so we can get infrastructure aligned:

Success criteria (as discussed)
- End-to-end latency under 350ms 95th for 1k concurrent users on typical prompts
- Stable throughput supporting ~120 QPS for embedding + generation mix
- No more than 2x cost relative to baseline target (tbd)
- Deterministic output for our canned eval set (will share)

Evaluation plan
- 2-week smoke + 4-week trial (recommended)
- Provide synthetic and subset of live traffic; run nightly batch of evals; measure latency, cost per token, and correctness on eval set
- Redwood to run baseline and optimized config (batching, KV cache, quantization profile)

Capacity ask / initial sizing (Lumina request)
- Baseline: 4 reserved GPUs (NVIDIA A100 equivalent) for steady-state testing
- Burst: autoscale to 12–16 GPUs for peak load (expected short bursts during demo/test windows)

Ownership / contacts
- Marissa (sales) — POC owner / commercial lead
- Vivek (SE) — technical lead and demo support
- Rishi (Infra) — capacity & infra provisioning

Next steps
1) Rishi: confirm whether Dedicated reserved + autoscale burst to shared pool is feasible and timing
2) Vivek: send mutual action plan and proposed timeline for kickoff
3) Alex: please share procurement contact and the eval script you want Redwood to run

Attachments: lumina_poc_requirements.xlsx (your traffic profile), redwood_poc_plan.pdf (POC template)

Thanks — I’ll follow up on the timeline once we confirm infra.
—

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: POC Capacity Planning - Redwood + Lumina AI

Alex / Marissa —

We can support the configuration you described. Options and trade-offs below:

1) Dedicated Reserved Pool (recommended for predictable perf + isolation)
- Reserve 4 GPUs (A100-equivalent) in a dedicated pool for the trial window.
- Autoscale policy: allow burst to shared Redwood pool up to 16 GPUs. Bursts will be throttled by shared capacity and may incur warm-up time.
- Pre-warming: we recommend a 15–30 minute pre-warm step for large model weights to avoid cold-start latency for first requests.

2) Shared Dedicated + Soft Reservation
- Reserve 2 GPUs and rely more on autoscale to handle peaks; lower baseline cost but higher variability on 99th/99.9th pctl latencies.

Operational notes
- KV cache and prefix caching will reduce token cost on repeat traffic; recommend enabling by default for the POC.
- If you need strict burst guarantees, we can set a temporary burst reservation (subject to availability and pricing uplift).

Attached: poc_capacity_options.pdf (detailed options + pricing bands).

Estimated timeline to provision dedicated reserved pool: 5 business days after signed SOW/commit. If you need faster access we can try to allocate from shared capacity (same-day in many regions but not guaranteed).

Let me know which option you'd like and I’ll start provisioning.
—
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
